politicalStatus.value: Dutch colony comprising Curaçao and its associated Caribbean islands

descriptions.value: The scholarly historical note identifies Curaçao en Onderhorigheden as the pre-1936 collective colonial name for Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Sint Eustatius, Sint Maarten and Saba. It is used for the later raw Netherlands Antilles label only in this colonial interval; modern autonomous-country status is not projected backward. Early wartime labels and later constitutional renaming remain uncurated.

politicalStatus.value: Department of the French Republic

descriptions.value: The law of 19 March 1946 transformed Guadeloupe from a colony into a French department. The archives document debate about implementation; formal departmental status is not treated as proof that local conditions immediately equalled mainland conditions. This narrow status core omits officeholders and changing mainland constitutional arrangements.

politicalStatus.value: Haitian state under United States military occupation

descriptions.value: US occupation constrained Haitian political and financial authority. The source states that the dissolved legislature did not meet again until 1929. This researched period stops before that institutional change and does not equate occupation with US annexation. Earlier Haitian competing northern/southern governments are not inferred from the singular raw label.

descriptions.value: Ulate assumed the presidency on 8 November 1949 after the new constitution entered force on 7 November. The formal order is not labelled unrestricted democratic participation; later amended constitutional text is not projected backward.

sources.title: Leeward Islands Act 1871
sources.usage: Body read: PDF pages 1–3, sections 2–8: six presidencies; island governments/councils; Governor, executive council and General Legislative Council. Assent is not assumed to be commencement; no precise commencement-day claim.

sources.title: Anguilla History
sources.usage: Body read: HTML fetched and read in isolated anguilla.html after certificate-chain failure; paragraph on 1830s union, freeholder representative to St Kitts assembly and 1958 federation. No exact union date or British-colonial origin date inferred.

sources.title: The History
sources.usage: Body read: History body: British colony until 1966, separate Legislative Council and Assembly since 1652, property franchise until 1950; ministerial government began 1 February 1954. No modern Senate projected backward.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Belize country study (public mirror)
sources.title: Crown Colony, 1871–1935
sources.usage: Body read: Complete three-paragraph body: appointed Governor and Council, reserve powers withheld until 1932; exact composition varied. 1932 transition date not specified, so accepted bounds stop before that year.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Belize country study (public mirror)
sources.title: Formal Establishment of the Colony, 1862–71
sources.usage: Body read: Full body: April 1871 constitution, lieutenant governor and appointed official/unofficial Legislative Council. Official embassy incorrectly calls 1862 Crown-colony date; constitutional study preferred for 1871 framework.

sources.title: Grenada report on implementation of recommendations, 2014
sources.usage: Body read: PDF page 3 paragraph 5 explicitly British Crown Colony 1877–1967. Grenada statistics poverty report gives 1879: do not select disputed first year; narrow researched interval 1900–1947, no exact founding-year claim. Modern government not used.

sources.title: Koloniaal en slavernijverleden van Gouda
sources.usage: Body read: PDF pages 166–167 colonial legislation discussion; page 225 note 2 identifies Curaçao en Onderhorigheden as pre-1936 name for six islands united as one colony. No 1800 or 1815 wartime mapping accepted.

sources.title: Antilles françaises research guide
sources.usage: Body read: Full body, colonial contemporary administration 1815–1946 and geographic series; linked island dependencies historically vary. Colonial frame only, no French mainland-government overlay.

sources.title: Échos de la départementalisation
sources.usage: Body read: Body paragraphs with law 19 March 1946 and Clartés newspaper 30 March 1946, declaring Guadeloupe French department; 1947 agricultural editorial and 1958 assimilation debate.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: US Invasion and Occupation of Haiti, 1915–34
sources.usage: Body read: Body paragraphs: US occupation, forced presidential selection and financial control, dissolved legislature did not meet again until 1929. Do not reuse inaccurate 1824 recognition statement; selected narrower 1918–1928 non-parliamentary occupation framework.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1958–1960 microfiche supplement: Haiti
sources.usage: Body read: Introduction body: President François Duvalier elected 1957 and dictatorship during 1958–1960 through National Police, Presidential Guard and secret police. No later presidency-for-life or 1964 constitution projected.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1951, Policy Statement, Dominican Republic
sources.usage: Body read: Body 17–20: Trujillo practical dictatorship since 1930; US military government 1916–24; sovereignty restored 1924 but financial supervision/debt distinct. Title of President not inferred for every Trujillo year.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1952–1954 Guatemala, Introduction
sources.usage: Body read: Body: Ubico unchecked powers, suspended constitutional guarantees after assuming 1931, relinquished 1 July 1944. Arévalo/Árbenz and 1954 history reviewed but not automatically merged into Ubico framework.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1952–1954, Reid memorandum, 12 June 1953
sources.usage: Body read: Body retrospective Carias dictatorship and provincial military supporters, 1949 Gálvez inauguration; footnote explicitly Carias ruled 1933–49. No institutional democratization inferred merely from presidential label.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, El Salvador country study (public mirror)
sources.title: Repression and Reform under Military Rule
sources.usage: Body read: Entire body: military rule, Martínez legislature confirmation in 1932, election 1935 and 1939, May 1944 resignation. 1934–35 interruption/1939 constitutional changes not smoothed; narrow 1936–1939 pre-new-term profile.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1951, Policy Statement, Nicaragua
sources.usage: Body read: Body background: Anastasio Somoza practical control since 1936 via National Guard and presidential terms; opposition ineffective. No uninterrupted formal presidency or precise beginning assumed.

sources.institution: Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones, Carolina Mora Chinchilla
sources.title: Las elecciones olvidadas: 1948 a 1949
sources.usage: Body read: Full historical article and quoted 1949 constituent decrees: Junta de facto legislative/executive powers, Ulate took presidency 8 November 1949, constitution entered force prior day, elected legislature/vice-presidents and exclusion of communists. Modern consolidated text not projected.

sources.institution: US Senate, Government Publishing Office historical translation
sources.title: Constitution of the Republic of Panama, Senate Document 208, 1904
sources.usage: Body read: PDF full constitutional body, Articles 1–3, 51–53, 70 and 136: republican nation with President, National Assembly and judicial branch, treaty jurisdictional limitations and US intervention clause. Accept basic formal frame 1914 only; no territorial claim to Canal Zone.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1958–1960 Cuba, Embassy telegram 430, 21 January 1960
sources.usage: Body read: Full telegram body: Prime Minister Fidel Castro and President Dorticós present in January 1960; revolutionary government, no modern Communist Party/1976 structure projected. Restricted researched month, not full office tenure.

limitations: Every accepted dossier is partial. No population, economic estimates, flags, exhaustive officials, predecessor/successor links or geometry-derived conclusions added.
Colonial dossier mappings identify an island/administrative framework, not a claim that it was a sovereign modern state.
Panama 1914 and Cuba January 1960 are deliberately narrow primary-document cores. Unresearched years remain gaps.
historicalCautions: Haiti 1815 competing governments are not inferred from the single raw map label.
Guadeloupe colonial status does not imply an unchanged French mainland government during World War II.
Netherlands Antilles raw name before 1936 resolves only to the independently sourced Curaçao collective colony; early war years remain gaps.
Trujillo and Somoza practical control is distinct from formal presidential tenure.
The Costa Rica constitution commenced 7 November 1949, while the accepted post-junta government mapping commences 8 November; no formal state-succession claim is made.
British Honduras embassy Crown-colony 1862 statement conflicts with detailed constitutional studies identifying April 1871; detailed Library of Congress study preferred.
